I'll think through this year's plan the way I always do — start from what I did last year and adjust for what I see in the soil and in fertilizer prices.

My 7.5 mu is mostly wheat-maize rotation, but I keep about 1 mu near the house for kohlrabi in spring. That patch brings in cash at the market and keeps something on the table. The other 6.5 mu stays in the wheat-maize double crop — it's what the land here does best, and the well irrigation makes it reliable.

**Winter wheat (6.5 mu):** Last year I got around 480 kg/mu, which is normal for our soil. I will put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at about 40 kg/mu as base before planting — that gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P₂O₅, 6 kg K₂O. Then I top-dress with 20 kg urea/mu at jointing — that's another 9 kg N. Total N about 15-16 kg/mu. I know from the extension station that our soil here has enough potassium so I don't push K higher. I irrigate three times: after sowing, before winter, and at jointing. Two pesticide sprays — one for aphids and one combined weed/fungus spray. Rotary tillage after maize stubble, I don't have time to deep plough every year.

**Summer maize (6.5 mu):** I do no-till direct seeding right after wheat harvest to save water and time. Zhengdan hybrid seed, I've used it for years. Base fertilizer 30 kg compound, then side-dress 20 kg urea at big trumpet stage. About 15 kg N total. Two irrigations usually — seedling and tasseling. Two sprays for corn borer and armyworm. I expect 550 kg/mu if the August rain comes normal.

**Spring kohlrabi (1 mu):** Vegetables eat fertilizer. I use more manure here, plus heavier NPK. About 20 kg N, 10 kg P, 15 kg K per mu, four irrigations, two sprays for flea beetles and aphids. Deep plough because vegetables need loose soil. I target about 3000 kg/mu of heads.

I keep a little extra fertilizer on wheat and maize — a bad harvest costs much more than a bag or two of urea.
